To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rationalities governing planning change over time and can be revealed by analysing the plans produced by planning agencies.
the discourse of plans in WA is characterized by a shift from the rationalities of “the city as a machine,” “the city as an organism,” “the city in the landscape,” and finally “the city as network.”
the discourse of plans in WA has been characterized by a shift from a rationalistic, modernist approach to planning in the 1950s and 1960s to a postmodernist approach in the 1980s and 1990s.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the changing discourses of city plans in the city of Perth, Western Australia, and the role of planning in that city over the last half century.
the changing discourse of city plans, and how these discourses reflect the rationalities of planning in WA.
the changing discourses of city plans, and how these reflect changing rationalities of planning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rationalities of planning in WA have changed from a modernist to a postmodern rationality.

the changing rationalities of planning in WA are: (a) the shift from a rational planning model to a communicative rationality model; and (b) the shift from the dominance of a modernist paradigm to a postmodern paradigm.

the plans of Perth, and indeed of other cities, are the product of the rationalities that prevail in the planning profession at the time of their production, and as such are the most important product of the profession.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
planning has become more complex, and more contested, as the city has grown, and as the role of planning has changed from a technical to a more political one.

the plans for Perth have become more complex, more inclusive, and more sophisticated over time, and that the rationalities of planning in the state of WA have become more diverse, less certain, and less stable.
, in Perth, the plan has evolved from a document of urban design to a document of urban governance, and from a document of the city to a document of the state.

the plan is an essential object of inquiry in the study of planning, and the analysis of its discourses is a useful way to understand the changing nature of planners’ roles, and the changing role of planning, over time.
